High purity niobium and aluminium were melted using a non-consumable tungsten electrode in a water cooled copper hearth into 40 mm diameter by 8 mm thick buttons: The buttons were flipped and remelted three times for homogeneity.
The buttons were cut into pieces using a diamond cutter and remelted into rectangular bars of dimensions 55 mm x 25 mm x 14 mm (thickness).
The cast materials were homogenization treated at 1900 “C for 3 h in the case of binary and for 5 h in the case of ternary material in a vacuum of better than 4 x 10 -4 Pa.
The homogenization treated block was isothermally forged at low strain rates at 1600 “C to approximately 50% of its original height in a vacuum of better than 4 x 10m4 Pa.
Isothermally forged materials were annealed at 1600 “C for 60 h in a vacuum of about 3 x 10m4 Pa.

conflicts.description: The abstract states that tantalum addition increases strength of Nbss/Nb3Al alloys, but the same paper's room-temperature hardness data show no significant contribution of Ta addition to room-temperature hardness; also the paper attributes the higher room-temperature strength of Nb-12Al-10Ta versus Nb-13Al partly to slightly higher Al in the A15 phase rather than solely to tantalum.

evidence.quote: The addition of tantalum improves the high-temperature strength of Nb,,/Nb,Al alloys.

The room temperature hardness of the binary Nb-11.8Al and Nb- 11.5A-9.9Ta is nearly the same, indicating no significant contribution of the tantalum addition of about 10 mol% to the room temperature hardness.

A slightly higher aluminium content in the Al5 phase of ternary material compared with the binary material may also contribute to the hardening of tantalum alloyed single-phase material. This might have caused the increased strength of Nb-12Al-1OTa compared with Nb-13Al at low temperatures.
